surface: CI, release and install scripts: workflows, build-app.sh, release.sh, make-appcast.sh, restart-app.sh, Homebrew cask
boundary: Workflow permissions and secret scoping, signing and entitlement checks, install swap

excluded_blocks.reason: no cloud deployment; release goes to GitHub Releases and a Homebrew cask

local_checks.invariant: Untrusted code (PRs, forks, branches) never runs with signing secrets or write tokens; tag-derived values never reach a shell as code
local_checks.result: release.yml triggers only on v* tag push, top-level permissions {}, build job has contents:read plus the 'release' environment, publish job has contents:write and no secrets and no checkout. ci.yml runs on push to main and pull_request with contents:read and no secrets. Every third-party action is pinned by SHA and the XcodeGen download is SHA-256 verified. The tag name only reaches the shell through env vars (GITHUB_REF_NAME), and release.sh re-validates the version with a regex before use. A tagged commit must be an ancestor of origin/main. No pull_request_target, no cache, no workflow_run. Reviewer gate on the 'release' environment and tag rules are repository settings not visible in source.

local_checks.invariant: A real release refuses wrong entitlements, unsigned or ad-hoc output, and a missing signing identity; failures stop the script
local_checks.result: release.sh uses set -euo pipefail, ':?' on SIGN_IDENTITY and NOTARY_PROFILE, compares the sorted entitlement key list to exactly the two expected keys (empty or failed codesign output fails closed), rejects get-task-allow, then codesigns the DMG, runs notarytool --wait, stapler staple (fails without a ticket) and spctl. The entitlements file declares exactly those two keys and hardened runtime is on in project.yml. The pipeline in build-app.sh keeps pipefail so an xcodebuild failure propagates. No fail-open path found.

local_checks.invariant: The tested dependency graph (Package.resolved) is the one compiled into the signed, notarized release app
local_checks.result: Only the four direct packages are exact-pinned in Package.swift; transitive packages (misakiswift, swift-argument-parser, swift-numerics, zipfoundation) are pinned only in the committed root Package.resolved. ci.yml 'swift test' (SwiftPM) honours that file, but the signed build goes through generated, gitignored PairVox.xcodeproj (local package path '.') with no -onlyUsePackageVersionsFromResolvedFile or -disableAutomaticPackageResolution and no step that places Package.resolved into the xcodeproj workspace. Whether Xcode reads the local package's root Package.resolved is not observable here, so this is a needs_validation candidate.

local_checks.invariant: Update metadata, install swap and cask bind to the signed artifact identity and fail closed
local_checks.result: Sparkle is not linked and SUFeedURL and SUPublicEDKey are empty, so no updater consumer exists in a shipped build (Updater.swift also requires an https feed). make-appcast.sh is an owner-run local script that signs with the login-Keychain EdDSA key. restart-app.sh is a same-UID developer convenience that verifies the signature structure before swapping. The Homebrew cask is a template with a placeholder sha256, which brew rejects, so it fails closed. Hardening notes recorded, no finding.

unresolved: Whether the GitHub Environment 'release' has required reviewers and a deployment-branch/tag policy, and whether a v* tag ruleset and main branch protection exist (repository settings, not in source).
Whether Xcode on the macos-15 runner honours the root Package.resolved of a local package referenced by path (see candidate).
parent_hardening: release.yml does not require a green ci.yml run for the tagged commit; add a status check (or run the tests in the build job) before the signing steps.

The main-ancestor check accepts any old main commit, so an older, weaker revision can be re-released under a new version number; require the tag to equal origin/main or use signed tags, and fail when CFBundleVersion would not exceed the previous release.
scripts/release.sh run locally does not check that HEAD is on main, the tree is clean, or the repo is not shallow (git rev-list --count HEAD feeds CFBundleVersion); add those checks.

ci.yml uses the mutable container tag swift:6.0, and both workflows use xcode-version latest-stable; pin by digest or version for reproducibility. No secrets are present in ci.yml, so this is not a release risk.

release.yml passes the notary app-specific password on the command line of notarytool store-credentials; the runner is ephemeral and the value is masked, but a stdin or prompt-free keychain-profile approach avoids ps exposure.
publish job has no 'release' environment and does not verify the DMG (spctl or stapler validate) or publish a SHA-256 file; the Homebrew sha256 is a manual copy from the log.

make-appcast.sh signs every dist/PairVox-*.dmg without checking notarization, staple, version match, or that DOWNLOAD_URL_PREFIX is https. Sparkle is not linked, so there is no consumer today; add checks before enabling it.
restart-app.sh swaps dist/PairVox.app with rm -rf then mv (non-atomic) and checks only 'codesign --verify', not a team or CDHash match; same-UID developer tool, availability-only.
packaging/homebrew/pairvox.rb has OWNER placeholders in url and homepage while the repo is arcwel/PairVox; fill them before publishing a tap. The placeholder sha256 makes brew fail closed.

PhoneModel.authenticate returns DeviceAuth.none for any canEvaluatePolicy failure, and approveByTap then still sends a tap approval for a high-risk request; the Mac ignores the field. Restrict the pass-through to LAError.passcodeNotSet and refuse high-risk taps otherwise.
KeychainCredentialStore items survive app deletion; add a first-launch marker (UserDefaults) that deletes an orphaned item after reinstall.

LinkClient.connect accepts an unauthenticated HandshakeRefusal (.unknownDevice, .revoked) as a permanent reason to stop retrying and tells the user to forget and re-pair; a peer able to answer on the Mac's address could use this to prompt a re-pair. Low risk on a tailnet.
isAllowedHost also accepts localhost and all of 127.0.0.0/8 in release builds; this is test support and only reaches the phone itself, but consider gating it behind a debug build flag.

surface: Local files: settings.json, paired-phones.json, phone-keys.json, logs, screech recordings, diagnostics bundles
boundary: File permissions, atomic replace, damaged-file handling and what is written to logs
selected_companion_blocks: DATA-ISOLATION-AND-LIFECYCLE.md#Deletion, revocation, and lifecycle attack classes

local_checks.invariant: A settings.json that another user could have written or that another user owns must not grant standing consents or name the program that receives the API key; damaged or unreadable settings must fail toward fewer privileges.
local_checks.result: SettingsStore.load() zeroes claudePathOverride, folderGrants, trustProjectConfiguration, autoApproveLowRisk, spokenHighRiskConfirmation, phoneLinkEnabled, voiceApprovesNeedsScreen and approveByVoiceFromSummary unless the file is owned by the current uid and has no group or other write bit (attributesOfItem uses lstat, so a planted symlink or a file made by another user fails the owner check). A decode failure returns defaults, which are the least-privilege values. save() writes atomically and sets 0600, and creates a missing folder at 0700. The remaining gaps need write access to a file inside the 0700 PairVox folder under the 0700 Application Support folder, so no lower-trust principal reaches them (see hardening). No candidate.

local_checks.invariant: Phone keys and the paired-phone list are private (0600 in a 0700 folder), replaced atomically, revoked keys are destroyed and cannot be resurrected from a restored or planted list, and a damaged file is kept aside instead of being overwritten.
local_checks.result: FileDeviceKeyStore and PairingManager.write create the temporary file at 0600 in a folder re-chmodded to 0700, then replaceItemAt; phone-keys.json is excluded from backup and stale .tmp files are removed at init. Unreadable files are moved aside, not overwritten. attach() accepts a key in the list file only once (legacy import marker, Keychain item or marker file), rejects non-UUID ids, and re-reads keys only for non-revoked entries, so restoring an old paired-phones.json cannot revive a revoked phone whose key was destroyed (Keychain items are ThisDeviceOnly). revoke() zeroes the in-memory key, removes the stored key, persists and surfaces failures. Documented same-user limits for development builds are in THREAT_MODEL.md. No candidate.

local_checks.invariant: Logs, recordings and exported diagnostics contain no credentials or pairing secrets, conversation text only with the owner's opt-in, and are not readable by a lower-trust local principal.
local_checks.result: Every log string field passes LogRedactor (API keys, GitHub and AWS tokens, bearer tokens, key=value secrets, e-mail, home path, account name). Conversation text is logged as a length unless logConversationText is on; contentFingerprint logs only a 16-hex SHA-256 prefix. Call sites reviewed in ConversationEngine, ClaudeCLISession, LinkHost, PhoneLinkModel and AppModel log tool names, lengths, ids and device names (sanitized) but never PSKs, pairing secrets, API keys or full commands. The control socket logs only the command name. Log folder and files are created with umask defaults (0755/0644 on a live Mac: ~/Library/Logs/PairVox) and PlaybackRecorder files are never chmodded, but the parent ~/Library is 0700 so no other local user can reach them. FeedbackCatcher writes 0600 files in a folder it creates at 0700 only if absent, and prunes to 10 pairs. Exporter stages in the per-user temp folder and removes it; playback audio is exported only if the owner enabled recording. No candidate.

parent_hardening: DiagnosticLog.openIfNeeded creates ~/Library/Logs/PairVox and pairvox*.log with umask defaults (live: drwxr-xr-x / -rw-r--r--), and PlaybackRecorder (AudioDiagnostics.swift:303-320) creates playback-*.caf (room speech, up to 15 min per start, 172 MB observed) the same way and never prunes them. FeedbackCatcher already uses 0700/0600. Not exploitable while ~/Library is 0700; create the folder at 0700 and the files at 0600, and cap playback files by count or age.

SettingsStore.load zeroes the consent fields but not openProjects/lastProject/recentProjects (AppModel.swift:151-155 relaunches Claude in those folders at startup), nor does it keep macSecondConfirmation. A settings.json that is group or other writable could therefore choose which folder Claude opens in. Unreachable while the PairVox folder is 0700 and the file is 0600; add the project list to the zeroed set for defence in depth.

SettingsStore.save only sets 0700 on a folder it creates (an existing folder is left as is), and the .atomic temporary file is created with the default mode before the 0600 chmod. PairingManager.write and FileDeviceKeyStore.prepareDirectory re-chmod the folder, so the folder ends up 0700 after the first pairing; ModelStore.ensureKokoro and WhisperModelStore create PairVox/Models with createDirectory and no mode. Chmod the folder in SettingsStore.save too and write the temporary file at 0600.
A damaged settings.json is replaced by the next save (no .unreadable aside copy), unlike paired-phones.json and phone-keys.json, which are moved aside.

paired-phones.unreadable-*.json and phone-keys.unreadable-*.json keep copies of old phone keys (legacy list format, or a truncated key file) and are never deleted after a revoke. They are not loaded, so they cannot authenticate, but they outlive revocation; delete them once the store decodes again, or at revoke.

FileDeviceKeyStore.load() treats any read failure (for example a transient EACCES or EMFILE) as a damaged file and moves it aside, which makes every paired phone look revoked until the owner pairs again. Distinguish a decode failure from an I/O error.

PairingManager.write does not remove its .paired-*.tmp file when replaceItemAt throws, and init does not sweep stale ones (phone-keys has such a sweep). The temp file carries no key when a key store is attached.

ModelStore.download uses URLSession(.default) and leaves a .part file in the model folder if the task fails after the move; neither store sweeps stale *.part files, and Kokoro has no free-space check before a 327 MB download. TTSProbe.run loads the Kokoro files after a size-only isPresent check instead of verifyKokoro().

The diagnostics ZIP lands on ~/Desktop (iCloud-synced when Desktop and Documents sync is on) with default permissions. Logs include project folder names and the child's cwd (project.switch, process.launched, settings.changed excludes path-bearing keys but these do not), although the README and system.json exclusion imply project places are left out. LogRedactor replaces only the home folder and account name.

collect-diagnostics.sh builds sed patterns from $HOME and $USER unescaped and uses -E, so an account name with regex characters leaves the path unredacted in crash reports; it also replaces a short $USER inside any word.

Outside this unit: AppModel.openTerminalForLogin (AppModel.swift:815-818) builds an AppleScript string from the claude path escaping only double quotes, not backslashes. The path comes from a PATH search or the validated override, so it is not attacker-reachable in the stated model, but quote it with a proper escape.

surface: Spoken input: transcripts while a request waits, voice commands, folder grants and the advisor text
boundary: Spoken-answer parsing, voice-command gating, folder grants and advisor output that must never read as an approval

excluded_blocks.reason: child spawn and argument injection are a separate unit

local_checks.invariant: A spoken reply counts as an approval only when it is an actual answer, given after the owner was told what the request is, and only while the request is fresh
local_checks.result: Two gaps. (1) permissionAnswer accepts any 5-word-or-shorter utterance that contains an approve word, and process() dispatches the parsed command before it reaches the 'question about the request' branch, so 'Is that okay?' approves. (2) pendingPermission is set the moment the request arrives, but nothing checks that its spoken prompt has played before a yes, okay or 'sounds good' counts. The age limit (300 s) and the voiceApprovable flag are enforced on every voice path (perform .approve, confirmHighRisk, announcements). The allow-all second pass skips the age check for armed ids, which is low impact and listed under hardening.

local_checks.invariant: A folder shell grant covers only commands whose every file reference resolves inside the granted folder
local_checks.result: shellGrant resolves symlinks only for tokens that contain a slash, start with a tilde or equal '..'. A bare file name that is a repository symlink to an outside file (cat notes) is never resolved, so the command is rated low, passes every disqualifier and is covered. The Read tool treats the same path as outside the project and asks. Edit grants resolve symlinks correctly. The offer flow keeps the two-step answers, refuses the home folder, '/' and any folder holding PairVox or Claude configuration, and gives the owner a text that matches what is granted apart from the code-execution caveat noted in hardening.

local_checks.invariant: Advisor output can never approve, deny or edit a request, and advisor text read aloud cannot work as a spoken approval
local_checks.result: The advisor is a separate one-shot claude -p call with Read, Grep and Glob only, no MCP, user-level settings and a fenced request block, and it has no handle on the session. Advisor text is passed through speakableAdvice on the explain, question and summary paths and in the cross-project recap. permissionPrompt appends the raw explanation unfiltered on re-prompts (hardening). Model prose and the Bash description narration are spoken with no approval-phrase filter; this only matters if echo cancellation fails and is listed under hardening.

parent_hardening: Allow-all second pass (ConversationEngine.perform .approveAllWaiting, lines 887-908): approveAllWaiting(requestIDs:) approves the armed ids without re-checking age or content. The guard only requires some other fresh eligible request to exist, so armed requests that went stale between the two 'allow all' utterances can still be approved. Re-filter the armed ids by isStale and voiceApprovable at the second pass and give the arming a time limit.

ConversationEngine.permissionPrompt (line 1234) appends the raw advisor explanation to the spoken prompt on re-prompts; every other site passes advisor text through speakableAdvice. Apply speakableAdvice there too.

Model-authored text spoken aloud with no approval-phrase filter: assistant prose, the Bash 'description' narration (ToolNarrator, up to 60 characters) and WebSearch queries. Only advisor text is filtered. If echo cancellation fails (the app already warns when it is unavailable) the model can say 'confirm high risk' or 'sounds good'. Consider filtering all spoken model text with the same predicate and ignoring any utterance whose speech began while the output was playing.

WebFetch is rated medium and voice-approvable, while any network-reaching Bash command is screen-only. The spoken text gives only the host; the path and query (an exfiltration channel) are not read. Consider making WebFetch screen-only or reading the full URL path length and query presence.

Folder grant text promises that commands which 'use the network or install things will still ask', but the shell grant covers interpreter and build commands (python3 script.py, make, swift build, git commit) and the edit grant lets the model write the script first, so the two grants together allow unattended arbitrary code including network use. Say so in the offer text, or require a click for a command that runs a file the model wrote in the same session.

isSensitivePath names /.git/config but not /.git/hooks; hook files are untracked, so they do not show in git status or diff. Add /.git/hooks (and .git/info/exclude) to the high-risk path needles so edit grants never cover them.

Auto-approve of Grep/Glob with no path argument reads the whole project, including .env files, while an explicit Read of .env is rated sensitive (medium). Treat a path-less Grep as medium when the project contains sensitive files, or document the gap.

ClaudeAdvisor runs with the owner's user-level settings; if those allow reads outside the project (an allow rule, additionalDirectories or a permissive default mode), an injected request could make the advisor read and speak outside files. Run the advisor with an explicit --permission-mode default and --disallowedTools for non-project reads, or document the dependency.

setFolderGrants and setPronunciation rebuild the policy but do not re-assess the request already on screen, so a revoked grant or changed rule does not alter the displayed assessment until the next request. Re-assess pending and queued requests as setApproveByVoiceFromSummary already does.

A folder-grant offer stays open until some other utterance arrives, with no age limit; any two spoken words ('yes', then 'confirm') from the room persist a standing edit grant. Expire the offer after a short window and require the owner's click in the app for the final confirmation.

local_checks.invariant: A shell command that does something documented as high risk (recursive or forced rm, sudo, push) is rated high however it is spelled or wrapped, and a command that touches PairVox or Claude configuration is rated high under every spelling
local_checks.result: Two classifier gaps. (a) The structural pass looks only at the first program of each segment; wrapperNames skips only env, command, nohup, time, nice, exec, builtin, caffeinate and stdbuf and never skips their options, and timeout, xargs, sh -c and similar are not looked through. The text rules cover only short flags followed by whitespace, so 'timeout 60 rm --recursive --force build', 'env -i rm --recursive --force build' and 'ls | xargs rm -rf' (flag at end of string) come out medium. (b) touchesProtectedFolder compares paths with FolderScope.resolved, which does not fold case, on a case-insensitive default macOS volume, so ~/.CLAUDE or a lower-case 'pairvox' folder name is not matched. The Write and Edit path uses lower-cased needles and is not affected. The .approve guard itself (voiceApprovable false for high risk, screen-only, requires-interaction and stale) is sound.

Allow?'. The card shows only the summary, and no app view renders request.input. The arguments (recipient, body, target) are visible to nobody except the AI explanation, which is optional and model-written.

surface: Child process launch: settings, project folder, claude path discovery, environment, and API key
boundary: API key handling and never touching Claude.ai credentials

local_checks.invariant: The API key lives only in the Keychain and the child environment; it is never written to settings, logs or argv, and no Claude.ai credential is read or forwarded.
local_checks.result: Held. KeychainStore holds the key (kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlocked); AppModel.openProject reads it per launch and passes AuthMode.apiKey; LaunchConfiguration.environment() sets ANTHROPIC_API_KEY only after ChildEnvironment.filter; ClaudeCLISession logs only argv flags beginning with '--', the exe path and the cwd, never the env; no interpolation or dump of LaunchConfiguration/AuthMode exists in Sources. The key is not in argv (stdin stream-json; advisor argv carries only the clipped request). No code reads ~/.claude credentials (SessionCatalog reads only project session JSONL previews, UUID-validated). Residual: the key sits in the env of a child whose Bash tool is model-directed (see candidate).

local_checks.invariant: Secrets in child stderr, auth errors and the diagnostics bundle are scrubbed before they are written or exported.
local_checks.result: Held for the key shape: every log string passes LogRedactor (sk-ant-, sk-, gh tokens, AKIA, Bearer, key=value, e-mail, home path, user name); stderrTail is cut to 400 chars and scrubbed in the log; the exporter scrubs system.json and crash reports and omits path-bearing settings (claudePathOverride). Log files are created with default permissions (no 0600) under ~/Library/Logs/PairVox, protected only by ~/Library being 0700 (hardening). The authProblem text is shown unredacted in the local UI only.

local_checks.invariant: Nothing the model can run without the owner seeing it can read the API key out of the child environment.
local_checks.result: Not held in API-key mode with a shell folder grant: ChildEnvironment keeps the key in the child env by design; BashRisk has no rule for environment disclosure (env, printenv, export, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY); a bare 'printenv' or 'env' rates medium ('Not a recognized read-only command.'), which FolderScope.shellGrant does not disqualify, so it is covered by the grant and auto-approved. Whether Claude Code's Bash tool inherits the child's env is a CLI fact outside source, so recorded as needs_validation. ChildEnvironment itself matches its documentation (ANTHROPIC_*, CLAUDE_CODE_*, CLAUDECODE, CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, NODE_*, SSL_CERT_* dropped, applied to session, advisor, --version and CLI).

parent_hardening: BashRisk: add a high-risk rule for environment disclosure (env, printenv, export -p, set, /proc/*/environ, and any mention of ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or other *_KEY/_TOKEN names) and add that reason to FolderScope.shellDisqualifiers; consider passing the key through a file descriptor or Claude Code's apiKeyHelper instead of a plain environment variable.

ClaudeLocator: PATH- and directory-discovered claude binaries skip overrideProblem entirely; apply the same owner/mode checks to the discovered binary, check ancestors and group-write on the parent, and re-run the check at spawn time (AppModel.openProject uses the path cached at setup).

AppModel.openTerminalForLogin escapes only a double quote in claudePath and puts it unquoted into a Terminal shell command; a path with a backslash, space or shell metacharacter breaks or alters the command. Use 'quoted form of' with a shell-quoted path. Impact needs control of the override path or a PATH directory, so same-UID only.

ChildEnvironment is a deny-list: consider also dropping DYLD_*, NODE_PATH, BUN_OPTIONS, SSLKEYLOGFILE, REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE and CURL_CA_BUNDLE, or switch to an allow-list. All are set by the owner's own shell, so this is defense in depth.

KeychainStore.saveAPIKey deletes the old item before SecItemAdd; if the add fails the old key is lost, yet AppModel.saveAPIKey tells the user 'nothing changed'. Use SecItemUpdate or add before delete. Consider kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlockedThisDeviceOnly so the key does not move through backups or migration.

pairvox-cli --api-key-env VAR forwards VAR to the child as an ordinary variable as well as ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (the deny-list only covers ANTHROPIC_ and CLAUDE_CODE_ names); drop VAR from the child environment.
DiagnosticLog creates log files with default permissions and no explicit 0600/0700 (protected only by ~/Library being 0700); set modes explicitly, especially when conversation text logging is on.

ClaudeAdvisor passes the request text (up to 6000 characters of tool input, which can contain secrets typed into commands) in argv after '--', visible to other local users via ps; send it on stdin instead.

LineBuffer.append copies the whole pending buffer for each line (quadratic on large bursts); a 64 MB line cap with a child that streams many small lines could stall the reader. Low priority, child is semi-trusted.

local_checks.invariant: An approval from a phone is accepted only for a request that is in the host's latest snapshot, was handed to that same connection, and was not cut for size; the request is bound by (project, requestID) and the engine re-checks the ID.
local_checks.result: Held. approvalRefusal (LinkHost.swift:443-460) requires find() to match the latest bounded snapshot, refuses request.truncated before the tap early-return, and requires c.presented[key], which is per Connection and set only when a snapshot carrying that key is drained to that connection. key() is project-qualified and identical at publish, push and check time, including when a request moves between 'request' and 'others' on a Mac project switch. engine.approve is called with projectID ?? latest.activeProjectID evaluated in the same synchronous step as the check, and ConversationEngine.approvePending (ConversationEngine.swift:346-349) ignores a request whose ID is not the pending one, so a stale or replayed approve is a no-op. local_checks.invariant: A phone spoken answer cannot approve anything the Mac's voice rules would not (high risk, screen-only, stale), and remote text can never act as an answer to a waiting request.

The Pair dialog makes 'Pair' the default (Return) button, is floating, and calls NSApp.activate(ignoringOtherApps:) (PairConfirmationPanel.swift:30-37, 70). local_checks.invariant: Pre-auth connections are bounded in count (3 per peer, 8 total), time (10 s first frame, 10 s auth frame, 10 s ack) and bytes (1 MiB + 64 per frame), and every counted slot is released on every exit path
local_checks.result: Counts increment before any read and release through one defer plus a one-shot release on authentication, with no double release or leak path. A slow-drip first frame is cut by Self.within(preAuthTimeout) which closes the transport. The challenge, refusal and grant sends are a few hundred bytes. Frame length is checked before allocation. Worst case pre-auth memory is about 8 MiB. Weakness: the per-peer key is the TCP source address, which collapses to 127.0.0.1 behind a loopback forward (candidate link-host-preauth-peer-key-collapses-behind-loopback-forward). With distinct tailnet addresses, three peers can still hold all 8 slots (hardening)

local_checks.invariant: Post-auth state and queues are bounded per connection (outbox 32, snapshots 400 KB, 3 connections per device) and cleaned up on disconnect, revocation, send failure and shutdown
local_checks.result: Outbox is capped at 32 and snapshots replace each other; the single writer is dropped on a 10 s send timeout; connections are removed on loop exit, drop, shutdown and watchdog idle. LinkSnapshot.bounded cuts every text field and shrinks the transcript to fit 400 KB. Only paired phones reach these paths. Minor: Connection.presented is never pruned (bounded by distinct request ids per connection lifetime). Not a finding

parent_hardening: LinkHost.serve has no connection-rate limit or per-source backoff. Three distinct tailnet peers (or one peer plus loopback) can hold all 8 pre-auth slots by reconnecting every 10 s. Consider a short rejection window per source and a reserved slot for known device ids.

serveSession has no failure counter for bad handshake proofs or unknown device ids (not exploitable: 122-bit UUID ids and a 256-bit PSK), but logging or capping repeated failures per source would aid detection.
pairingKey(material) is used both as the HMAC key for the pair-request proof and the ChaChaPoly key for the grant; derive separate subkeys per purpose.

PairAck is an unauthenticated plaintext flag. Sending it keeps a device paired even if the key was never opened; harmless today because only a holder of the offer secret reaches that point, but an HMAC over the client nonce would make delivery provable.

PairingManager.attach imports legacy file keys without enforcing a 32-byte length (key(for:) later rejects non-32 byte keys, yet the in-memory device keeps the planted psk and activeDevice returns it). Reject psk.count != 32 at import. The import is gated by legacyImportClosed, whose marker is owned by the DeviceKeyStore peer unit.

servePairing revokes every device not present in its `before` snapshot when the ack fails. If a second pairing completed during that window, the wrong device could be revoked. Revoke by the specific id returned from redeem instead.
A pairing connection holds a pre-auth slot while waiting for the owner click (up to 150 s), but only a holder of the offer secret can reach that state.
LinkHost.Connection.presented is never pruned for the life of a connection; cap or expire entries.

Pair-request proof is not bound to the host or port, so a captured unredeemed request could be raced by an on-path observer to burn the one-time offer. Not reachable over the encrypted tailnet; consider including a host-chosen nonce in the proof.

surface: Model downloads: Kokoro and Whisper files fetched at runtime
boundary: SHA-256 and size pins, unknown-variant refusal, partial download handling

local_checks.invariant: Kokoro weights and voices are loaded only after the whole file matches the in-source SHA-256 and size, whatever the download host or redirect returns; a failed or partial download is discarded and fails closed.
local_checks.result: The trusted root is the pin compiled into the app (ModelStore.kokoroWeights/kokoroVoices), not anything fetched. The URLs use the mutable main branch, but ensureKokoro hashes the .part file before moveItem, deletes it and throws checksumMismatch on a mismatch, and VoiceStack.prepareKokoro runs verifyKokoro on an existing file before KokoroSynthesizer.load (the loader traps on malformed input). HTTP non-2xx ends the download without a move. Redirect hosts cannot change the outcome because only the hash decides. Gaps are availability or developer-only (hardening): an orphaned .part file if the task fails after the move, and --tts-probe loads after a size-only isPresent check.

local_checks.invariant: Only pinned Whisper variants are fetched, at an immutable commit, with per-file size and SHA-256 checks, a pinned path cannot leave the model folder, and WhisperKit cannot fetch anything itself.
local_checks.result: ensure(variant:) throws notPinned for a name not in WhisperPins.variants; Settings decoding also replaces an unknown whisperModel with the default. URLs are built from a 40-hex commit in source, so there is no moving branch. Every file is size- and hash-checked in the .part file before moveItem, and existing files are re-hashed at each load. destination(for:) rejects absolute, empty, '.' and '..' segments and checks the standardized prefix. WhisperKitConfig uses download: false with explicit modelFolder and tokenizerFolder. The pin generator validates path segments, commit and digest formats from upstream before writing Swift source. Pins for non-LFS files are computed from the same host at generation time (trust on first use at pin time), which is a pinning-process note, not a handoff failure. No candidate.

parent_hardening: DiagnosticLog.openIfNeeded creates ~/Library/Logs/PairVox and pairvox*.log with umask defaults (live: drwxr-xr-x / -rw-r--r--), and PlaybackRecorder (AudioDiagnostics.swift:303-320) creates playback-*.caf (room speech, up to 15 min per start, 172 MB observed) the same way and never prunes them. FeedbackCatcher already uses 0700/0600. Not exploitable while ~/Library is 0700; create the folder at 0700 and the files at 0600, and cap playback files by count or age.

SettingsStore.load zeroes the consent fields but not openProjects/lastProject/recentProjects (AppModel.swift:151-155 relaunches Claude in those folders at startup), nor does it keep macSecondConfirmation. A settings.json that is group or other writable could therefore choose which folder Claude opens in. Unreachable while the PairVox folder is 0700 and the file is 0600; add the project list to the zeroed set for defence in depth.

SettingsStore.save only sets 0700 on a folder it creates (an existing folder is left as is), and the .atomic temporary file is created with the default mode before the 0600 chmod. PairingManager.write and FileDeviceKeyStore.prepareDirectory re-chmod the folder, so the folder ends up 0700 after the first pairing; ModelStore.ensureKokoro and WhisperModelStore create PairVox/Models with createDirectory and no mode. Chmod the folder in SettingsStore.save too and write the temporary file at 0600.
A damaged settings.json is replaced by the next save (no .unreadable aside copy), unlike paired-phones.json and phone-keys.json, which are moved aside.

paired-phones.unreadable-*.json and phone-keys.unreadable-*.json keep copies of old phone keys (legacy list format, or a truncated key file) and are never deleted after a revoke. They are not loaded, so they cannot authenticate, but they outlive revocation; delete them once the store decodes again, or at revoke.

FileDeviceKeyStore.load() treats any read failure (for example a transient EACCES or EMFILE) as a damaged file and moves it aside, which makes every paired phone look revoked until the owner pairs again. Distinguish a decode failure from an I/O error.

PairingManager.write does not remove its .paired-*.tmp file when replaceItemAt throws, and init does not sweep stale ones (phone-keys has such a sweep). The temp file carries no key when a key store is attached.

ModelStore.download uses URLSession(.default) and leaves a .part file in the model folder if the task fails after the move; neither store sweeps stale *.part files, and Kokoro has no free-space check before a 327 MB download. TTSProbe.run loads the Kokoro files after a size-only isPresent check instead of verifyKokoro().

The diagnostics ZIP lands on ~/Desktop (iCloud-synced when Desktop and Documents sync is on) with default permissions. Logs include project folder names and the child's cwd (project.switch, process.launched, settings.changed excludes path-bearing keys but these do not), although the README and system.json exclusion imply project places are left out. LogRedactor replaces only the home folder and account name.

collect-diagnostics.sh builds sed patterns from $HOME and $USER unescaped and uses -E, so an account name with regex characters leaves the path unredacted in crash reports; it also replaces a short $USER inside any word.

Outside this unit: AppModel.openTerminalForLogin (AppModel.swift:815-818) builds an AppleScript string from the claude path escaping only double quotes, not backslashes. The path comes from a PATH search or the validated override, so it is not attacker-reachable in the stated model, but quote it with a proper escape.

surface: iPhone app: pairing link or QR scan, stored credentials, Face ID approvals, speech and audio
boundary: Phone-side credential storage, pairing-link parsing, Face ID gate before approving

excluded_blocks.reason: no webview in the phone app per recon

local_checks.invariant: No other app, page or intent can invoke a pairing or state-changing route without in-app user action
local_checks.result: Info.plist declares no CFBundleURLTypes, no associated domains and no document types, and the app has no onOpenURL or userActivity handler, so pairvox:// is not an OS-routable entry point. Pairing input comes only from the in-app QR scanner (metadata type .qr) or a PasteButton paste, both ending in an explicit 'Pair with host:port?' confirmationDialog. The clipboard is read only through PasteButton. Duplicate query fields resolve to the first value but are unreachable by third parties.

local_checks.invariant: A phone only pairs with, and only later reconnects to, a Tailscale-network host (PairingPayload.isAllowedHost)
local_checks.result: The IPv4 branch parses four numeric octets, but the IPv6 branch accepts any string that contains ':' and starts with 'fd7a:115c:a1e0:' without parsing an address, and the character filter allows letters, digits, '.', '-' and ':'. 'fd7a:115c:a1e0:x.attacker.example' therefore passes parse() and pair(). The IPv4 branch also accepts leading-zero octets such as '100.070.0.1' (Int -> 70) while a BSD-style resolver would read '070' as octal 56. The existing test list covers neither form. Candidate recorded.

local_checks.invariant: Stored credentials are device-bound and not synced, backed up or restored; pairing proofs bind the one-time secret
local_checks.result: KeychainCredentialStore uses a generic-password item with kSecAttrSynchronizable false and kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlockedThisDeviceOnly, so it is excluded from iCloud Keychain and device migration. save() updates in place so a failed save keeps the old key. Pairing material must be exactly 16 bytes, the grant is ChaCha20-Poly1305 sealed under an HKDF key from that secret with the phone nonce as AAD, and connect() checks the host proof before sending its own. Residual: the Keychain item survives app deletion and a reinstall auto-reconnects (hardening).

local_checks.invariant: A Face ID or passcode confirmation applies to the exact request displayed, and a stale or replaced request is not approved
local_checks.result: approveByTap captures the LinkRequest, runs LAContext .deviceOwnerAuthentication, then re-checks stillWaiting (requestID, live link, fresh snapshot, project) before sending requestID; the voice 'confirm high risk' path additionally refuses auth == .none. LinkHost.approvalRefusal requires the request to have been shown on that connection. The DeviceAuth field is phone-asserted and the Mac never relies on it (documented in LinkMessages.swift), so the gate is a phone-local presence check, not a cross-boundary control. No pending-action confusion found. Background Curtain overlay hides the transcript in the app switcher.

local_checks.invariant: Speech stays on the phone and frames from an unauthenticated peer are bounded
local_checks.result: SFSpeechAudioBufferRecognitionRequest.requiresOnDeviceRecognition is true and the code throws if on-device recognition is unavailable. TCPTransport caps frames at FrameCodec.maxFrameBytes + 64 before allocating. Logs print only error descriptions, never keys. Only text is sent over the link.

unresolved: Whether iOS Network.framework resolves a name such as 'fd7a:115c:a1e0:x.attacker.example' (colon in a DNS label) and whether the system resolver reads '100.070.0.1' as octal; both need a device or simulator run.

parent_hardening: release.yml does not require a green ci.yml run for the tagged commit; add a status check (or run the tests in the build job) before the signing steps.

The main-ancestor check accepts any old main commit, so an older, weaker revision can be re-released under a new version number; require the tag to equal origin/main or use signed tags, and fail when CFBundleVersion would not exceed the previous release.
scripts/release.sh run locally does not check that HEAD is on main, the tree is clean, or the repo is not shallow (git rev-list --count HEAD feeds CFBundleVersion); add those checks.

ci.yml uses the mutable container tag swift:6.0, and both workflows use xcode-version latest-stable; pin by digest or version for reproducibility. No secrets are present in ci.yml, so this is not a release risk.

release.yml passes the notary app-specific password on the command line of notarytool store-credentials; the runner is ephemeral and the value is masked, but a stdin or prompt-free keychain-profile approach avoids ps exposure.
publish job has no 'release' environment and does not verify the DMG (spctl or stapler validate) or publish a SHA-256 file; the Homebrew sha256 is a manual copy from the log.

make-appcast.sh signs every dist/PairVox-*.dmg without checking notarization, staple, version match, or that DOWNLOAD_URL_PREFIX is https. Sparkle is not linked, so there is no consumer today; add checks before enabling it.
restart-app.sh swaps dist/PairVox.app with rm -rf then mv (non-atomic) and checks only 'codesign --verify', not a team or CDHash match; same-UID developer tool, availability-only.
packaging/homebrew/pairvox.rb has OWNER placeholders in url and homepage while the repo is arcwel/PairVox; fill them before publishing a tap. The placeholder sha256 makes brew fail closed.

PhoneModel.authenticate returns DeviceAuth.none for any canEvaluatePolicy failure, and approveByTap then still sends a tap approval for a high-risk request; the Mac ignores the field. Restrict the pass-through to LAError.passcodeNotSet and refuse high-risk taps otherwise.
KeychainCredentialStore items survive app deletion; add a first-launch marker (UserDefaults) that deletes an orphaned item after reinstall.

LinkClient.connect accepts an unauthenticated HandshakeRefusal (.unknownDevice, .revoked) as a permanent reason to stop retrying and tells the user to forget and re-pair; a peer able to answer on the Mac's address could use this to prompt a re-pair. Low risk on a tailnet.
isAllowedHost also accepts localhost and all of 127.0.0.0/8 in release builds; this is test support and only reaches the phone itself, but consider gating it behind a debug build flag.
